title: JAH experiment: cell 5 borrows the other operators' values
t: JAH experiment: cell 5 borrows the other operators' values
description: JAH swaps cell 5's Sobel value for Prewitt's and Scharr's: the measured response shifts, live.
cell_role: Cell 5 (center) of the 3x3 kernel grid weights the pixel the pixel being processed itself. Sobel Gx 0, Sobel Gy 0; Prewitt Gx 0, Prewitt Gy 0; Scharr Gx 0, Scharr Gy 0. It is silent in both Sobel gradient estimates -- the pivot cell.
demo_code:
# Nine-number kernel lab -- pure-Python 3x3 convolution, zero dependencies.
# Images are 2-D brightness lists; the demo convolves the interior 3x3.
SOBEL_GX = [[-1,0,1],[-2,0,2],[-1,0,1]]
SOBEL_GY = [[-1,-2,-1],[0,0,0],[1,2,1]]
PREWITT_GX = [[-1,0,1],[-1,0,1],[-1,0,1]]
PREWITT_GY = [[-1,-1,-1],[0,0,0],[1,1,1]]
SCHARR_GX = [[-3,0,3],[-10,0,10],[-3,0,3]]
SCHARR_GY = [[-3,-10,-3],[0,0,0],[3,10,3]]
V = [[10,10,10,200,200] for _ in range(5)]   # vertical step edge: dark left, bright right
H = [[10]*5,[10]*5,[10]*5,[200]*5,[200]*5]   # horizontal step edge: dark top, bright bottom
F = [[50]*5 for _ in range(5)]               # flat field: no edges at all
D = [[10,10,10,10,10],[10,10,10,10,200],[10,10,10,200,200],[10,10,200,200,200],[10,200,200,200,200]]  # diagonal edge
def conv(img, k):
    return [[sum(img[y+dy-1][x+dx-1]*k[dy][dx] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3))
             for x in range(1,4)] for y in range(1,4)]
def show(m):
    for row in m:
        print(" ".join("%8g" % v for v in row))
r, c = 1, 1
for name, v in [('sobel',SOBEL_GX[r][c]),('prewitt',PREWITT_GX[r][c]),('scharr',SCHARR_GX[r][c])]:
    k = [row[:] for row in SOBEL_GX]; k[r][c] = v
    print("cell borrowed from %s (value %3d): Gx edge response at (2,2) = %d" % (name, v, conv(V,k)[1][1]))
demo_output:
cell borrowed from sobel (value   0): Gx edge response at (2,2) = 760
cell borrowed from prewitt (value   0): Gx edge response at (2,2) = 760
cell borrowed from scharr (value   0): Gx edge response at (2,2) = 760
body:
JAH's first laboratory experiment on cell 5 (center): keep the whole Sobel Gx kernel exactly as designed, but borrow this one cell's value from each of the other operators in turn, and measure the edge response on the standard vertical step edge. With Sobel's own 0 the response is 760; with Prewitt's 0 it becomes 760 (a shift of 0); with Scharr's 0 it becomes 760 (a shift of 0).

The finding: a single cell's 'opinion' moves the whole detector's answer by exactly its weight times its pixel -- no interaction effects, no surprises, pure linearity. That linearity is what makes kernel design honest work: every number can be judged on its own contribution. The executed demo performs the three-way borrow live and prints the measured responses.

body:
JAH's fourth experiment: a fractional cell. The classic kernels use whole numbers, but nothing in the mathematics requires it, so JAH sets cell 5 (center) to 0.5 -- half a vote, where the design says silence -- and measures. Edge response: 760 with the designed cell, 765.0 with the fractional one (delta 5.0).

The result is unglamorous and important: fractions work fine. Convolution does not care whether a weight is an integer; the response simply scales. That is the door to tuned kernels -- once you accept fractional cells, every cell becomes a dial, and the nine-number grid becomes a design space instead of a monument. The executed demo measures the fractional setting live.

On the synthetic diagonal step edge the full Sobel kernels answer Gx 570 and Gy 570 at the test pixel. Diagonal edges are the honest test of a 3x3 operator: an axis-aligned edge only exercises half the kernel, but a diagonal makes every cell testify. JAH's seventh experiment: cell 5 (center) under noise. A flat field of brightness 100 gets a single hot noise spike of 255 placed exactly on the pixel this cell weights. With the full Sobel Gx kernel the test pixel answers 0; with this cell zeroed it answers 0. The noise gain carried by this one cell is 0 -- precisely its weight 0 times the spike's excess of 155.

This is the cost side of every kernel weight: the same number that gathers edge signal also gathers noise, at exactly the same rate. A weight of 2 hears twice the signal and twice the noise; that is why smoothing weights exist at all -- they buy signal faster than they buy noise by averaging. The executed demo plants the spike, runs both kernels, and prints the measured noise gain.

body:
Seven experiments on one number. Cell 5 (center) -- Sobel Gx value 0 -- taught JAH this: (1) borrowing Prewitt's or Scharr's value moves the edge answer by exactly weight-times-pixel; (2) switching the cell off changes the edge response by 0 and disturbs the flat-field balance; (3) doubling the weight doubles its contribution, and a silent cell given any voice immediately spends its pixel's brightness; (4) fractional weights work fine -- the nine numbers are a design space, not a monument; (5) sign is meaning -- a flipped cell testifies for the opposite transition; (6) on diagonal edges the same linear law holds, which is why the grid generalizes to any angle; (7) the cell's noise gain is 0, its weight times the spike -- every weight buys signal and noise at the same rate.

The verdict JAH records for this cell: it is smoothing weight 2 (Sobel) / 1 (Prewitt) / 10 (Scharr) times differencing sign 0 -- somebody's opinion about how much to trust this row of pixels, measured seven ways and confirmed every time. The executed demo replays the two headline measurements -- the switch-off delta and the noise gain -- as the certified summary.
